glosses: Droit qui se lève sur les personnes, les animaux, les marchandises, pour leur passage sur un chemin, sur un pont, sur une rivière, etc.

examples.text: Je conseille à Charon de doubler son droit de péage, à Pluton de faire la guerre contre Jupiter pour être le premier des dieux, attendu que Jupiter gouverne mal les hommes, et que l’empire des morts est plus étendu que celui des vivants.
Beaucoup de navires feront du charbon à Colon, et tous seront forcés de s'arrêter au port d'entrée pour acquitter le péage, prendre des pilotes.
Une surtout, le droit de péage dont les seigneurs prétendaient frapper la navigation du Ligneul, éternisa les querelles.

glosses: Redevance pour circuler sur les autoroutes et certains ponts.

examples.text: La plupart des routes européennes font l’objet désormais d’un péage, d’une taxe ou d’une redevance.

glosses: Lieu où l’on paye le droit de passage.

examples.text: Mon cœur s'emballait à chaque pont quand l’autobus s’arrêtait au péage. Avec l’angoisse montait aussi le remords.

glosses: A fee paid for some liberty or privilege, particularly for the privilege of passing over a bridge or on a highway, or for that of vending goods in a fair, market, etc.

examples.text: Meanwhile, the tolls dispute had gone to the courts, and the E.L.R. was completely successful when, in 1856, the House of Lords awarded it the sum of £30,000 against the L.Y.R. for tolls overcharged.

glosses: Loss or damage incurred through a disaster.

examples.text: The war has taken its toll on the people.

examples.text: We can handle on a toll basis your needs for spray drying, repackaging, crushing and grinding, and dry blending.

glosses: The act or sound of ringing a bell, especially slowly, as with a church or cemetery bell.
To ring (a bell) slowly and repeatedly.

examples.text: Martin tolled the great bell every day.
Ask not for whom the bell tolls.

From the belfries far and near the funereal deathbell tolled unceasingly while all around the gloomy precincts rolled the ominous warning of a hundred muffled drums punctuated by the hollow booming of pieces of ordnance.

glosses: To summon by ringing a bell.

examples.text: The ringer tolled the workers back from the fields for vespers.

When hollow murmurs of their evening bells

glosses: To announce by ringing a bell.

examples.text: The bells tolled the King’s death.

glosses: To make a sound as if made by a bell.

examples.text: The chaplain's first mention of the name Yossarian! had tolled deep in his memory like a portentous gong.

glosses: To draw; pull; tug; drag.

glosses: To lure with bait; tole (especially, fish and animals).

To suspend.
